British Values
Abbey View School Promoting British Values
At Abbey View School, we actively promote positive, inclusive values. These include democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, and mutual respect for and tolerance of those of different faiths and beliefs. We believe British values are those values expected of anyone living in Britain, regardless of their nationality, culture or religious belief.
Our ethos reflects these values. We place great emphasis on building positive relationships in school, amongst the students themselves and between staff and students. We strongly believe students should not merely be taught such values but that they are embedded into school life.
The information below reflects how Abbey View School works to promote positive values through the ethos and life of the school.
Promoting the value of Democracy
At Abbey View School, the principle of democracy is consistently reinforced, through student voice and through formal and informal discussions with all students. It also is promoted via the running of the school council.
Promoting the value of the Rule of Law
The importance of laws, whether they be those that govern the class, the school, or the country, are consistently reinforced throughout regular school days, as well as when dealing with behaviour. Students are taught the values and reasons behind laws, that they govern and protect us, the responsibilities that this involves and the consequences when laws are broken. Visits from authorities such as the Police and Fire Service help reinforce this message.
Promoting the value of Individual Liberty
Within Abbey View School students are actively encouraged to make independent choices knowing that they are in a safe, secure and supportive environment. As a school we educate and provide boundaries for students to make choices safety, through the provision of a safe environment and an empowering education. Students are encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights, responsibilities and personal freedoms and receive advice about how to exercise these safely.
Promoting the value of Mutual Respect
Respect is at the core of our school ethos and is modelled by students and staff alike. The school promotes respect for others and this is reiterated through our classroom and learning environments. In line with our commitment to democracy, students at Abbey View School are always able to voice their opinions in an appropriate manner and we foster an environment where students are safe to disagree with each other. Mutual respect is embraced throughout the school.
Promoting the value of Tolerance of those of different faiths, ideas and religions
This is achieved through equipping students with the ability to understand their place in a culturally diverse society and by giving them opportunities to experience such diversity within the school community.
Should you feel that the school is not meeting this requirement, you should contact the school office and request to express your concerns with the Principal. Likewise, if you feel that anyone working at the school is undermining these values you should report this to the Principal.

Our Purpose & Vision
Purpose
We’ve recently developed a new Purpose for Abbey View. It expresses who we are and what we want to achieve. It’s an essential part of who we are. We strive everyday to bring this alive for all of our students.
Vision
Our new Vision is fundamental to achieving successful outcomes for our students, no matter their ability or background. It expresses our desired outcome for every student who visits the school, whether on a short or long term placement.
Our Purpose and Vision document provides further information.
av purpose and vision.pdf
© 2026 | Legal Information
Website design by Greenhouse School Websites

Welcome
Welcome to Abbey View and thank you for your interest in our school. At Abbey View, we believe that the time spent here is an invaluable investment in each student’s future. Our school provides a specialised alternative provision environment tailored for students who face challenges in traditional settings, helping them overcome barriers to learning and achieve academic success. Most of our students successfully return to mainstream secondary education or transition smoothly to post-16 educational pathways.
Abbey View serves students at risk of disengagement and marginalisation in their mainstream school, offering them a renewed sense of purpose and re-engagement with their education and lives. Our purpose is solidly built around Supporting Students, Fulfilling Potential and Delivering a Future of Possibilities – whether attending for a short or extended period of time.
In collaboration with partner schools and families, Abbey View offers a welcoming, secure, and supportive environment that promotes emotional well-being and safe lifestyle choices. Our vision of Successful Transitions, A Safe Trusted Environment, Excitement Through Education and Future Ready has been developed to ensure that we:
ABOUT ABBEY VIEW
Abbey View is operated by CCT Learning – which is a single academy trust. During mid 2025, the school will merge into a supportive Multi Academy Trust, unleashing not only a new chapter for the school, but also new possibilities.
Places at Abbey View School are commissioned by the student’s secondary school and cannot be applied for directly by students or families. If you have any further questions please do not hesitate to contact us.

Attendance
If your child cannot attend on a particular day, please telephone the main school by 8:30am on (01684) 292829. Please contact us on each day that your child is absent, unless this is a longer-term issue known to the school and supported by medical documentation, as appropriate.
Please do not use the office@abbey-view.org.uk email to report a student absence. The only exception to this is if you need to inform us of details of a forthcoming medical appointment, and in this case by attaching a confirmation and proof of the appointment.

School Meals (Food Standards Agency Rating 5)
Students are offered a snack and drink during Tutor Time from 9.15am until 9.30am every morning.
Breakfast is provided at 10.55am during the morning break. Students are offered a variety of foods e.g. toast, fruit, yoghurt, cereal and occasionally eggs or croissants.
Lunchtime is between 12.40pm and 1.20pm. Students and staff eat together in the school dining room. The school provides a cooked lunch every day.
If your child has any dietary requirements then please let the school office know.
The cost of food provided is met by the school.
© 2026 | Legal Information

Dress Code
Abbey View School does not currently have a school uniform. However, we would like to clarify what our dress code expectations are for students.
Students may wear joggers, leggings, or jeans with a plain t-shirt, jumper, or hoodie.
There must be no offensive logos on any clothing.
Crop tops or any other clothing that exposes the skin of the torso must not be worn.
No underwear should be exposed.
Flip-flops, sliders, crocs, slippers, and similar, loose fitting footwear is not considered safe or appropriate for school. All footwear must be securely fastened. Footwear should also be appropriate for planned activities.
We appreciate your support.
